key_insight: A margin-based analysis explains how LoRA can retain prior knowledge while adapting to new tasks and enables MaLoRA, a training-free adapter-merging rule.
engineering_relevance: Regularization and margin-balanced adapter mixing offer principled controls for balancing task adaptation, knowledge retention, and multi-task performance.
method: Analyze ℓ₂-regularized LoRA in multiclass linear classification with near-orthogonal tasks.
Show that optimal adapters align with max-margin solutions in an intermediate regularization regime.
Derive mixing coefficients that balance task margins and maximize the margin over their union.
evidence_signal: Experiments on modern architectures and real vision and language classification datasets show MaLoRA matching or outperforming several adapter-merging baselines.
watch_item: The theoretical guarantees rely on linear classification and near-orthogonal tasks; they may not extend directly to nonlinear models or strongly overlapping tasks.
paper_title: A Margin Perspective on LoRA: Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting and Adapter Merging (MaLoRA)
